## 1. Purpose

This module closes the simulated-data workflow by comparing all seven genomic
prediction methods on exactly the same outer-assessment individuals defined in
M02:

- `GBLUP_A`, `GBLUP_AD`, and `GBLUP_ADE`;
- `ANN_0`, `ANN_L1`, `ANN_L2`, and `ANN_L1_L2`.

The comparison uses only predictions already produced in M03 and M04. No model
is refitted and no hyperparameter is selected here. The known **true simulated
genetic value** is the primary evaluation target; the **observed phenotype** is
reported as a secondary target because it also contains residual variation.

Three principles define the comparison:

- every method contributes the same 150 `Scenario x outer split` tasks;
- every task contains the same 200 held-out individuals for all methods;
- all 21 unordered method pairs are contrasted within the same outer splits.
  These paired summaries describe repeated cross-validation results and are not
  treated as tests based on 150 statistically independent replicates.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  cache = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

dir.create(
  "output/simulated/m05/figures",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)
```

## 2. Inputs and matched evaluation design

### 2.1 Saved model results

```{r packages-and-inputs}
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)

GBLUP_RESULTS_RDS <-
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_results.rds"
GBLUP_PREDICTIONS_RDS <-
  "output/simulated/gblup/simulated_gblup_predictions.rds"
ANN_RESULTS_RDS <-
  "output/simulated/ann/final/simulated_ann_results.rds"
ANN_PREDICTIONS_RDS <-
  "output/simulated/ann/final/simulated_ann_predictions.rds"

gr <- readRDS(GBLUP_RESULTS_RDS)
gp <- readRDS(GBLUP_PREDICTIONS_RDS)
ar <- readRDS(ANN_RESULTS_RDS)
ap <- readRDS(ANN_PREDICTIONS_RDS)

expected_gblup_models <- c(
  "GBLUP_A",
  "GBLUP_AD",
  "GBLUP_ADE"
)

expected_ann_models <- c(
  "ANN_0",
  "ANN_L1",
  "ANN_L2",
  "ANN_L1_L2"
)

model_order <- c(
  expected_gblup_models,
  expected_ann_models
)

model_labels <- c(
  "GBLUP-A",
  "GBLUP-AD",
  "GBLUP-ADE",
  "ANN-0",
  "ANN-L1",
  "ANN-L2",
  "ANN-L1+L2"
)

stopifnot(
  identical(sort(unique(gr$Model)), sort(expected_gblup_models)),
  identical(sort(unique(ar$Model)), sort(expected_ann_models)),
  nrow(gr) == 450L,
  nrow(gp) == 90000L,
  nrow(ar) == 600L,
  nrow(ap) == 120000L
)

input_summary <- data.frame(
  Object = c(
    "GBLUP task-by-model results",
    "GBLUP held-out predictions",
    "ANN task-by-model results",
    "ANN held-out predictions"
  ),
  Rows = c(nrow(gr), nrow(gp), nrow(ar), nrow(ap)),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

input_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Saved results entering the seven-model comparison",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The inputs contain 450 GBLUP task-by-model results, 600 ANN task-by-model
results, 90,000 GBLUP held-out predictions, and 120,000 ANN held-out
predictions. The comparison therefore operates on completed model outputs
rather than reconstructing either modeling branch.

### 2.2 Matched tasks and assessment individuals

The next block checks the observed comparison structure directly. Because the
current GBLUP `TaskID` is model-specific, cross-method matching deliberately uses
the model-independent outer-split keys (`Scenario`, `Repetition`, `Fold`, and
`SplitID`); prediction records additionally use the individual identifier `ID`.

```{r matched-design}
split_keys <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID"
)

prediction_keys <- c(
  split_keys,
  "ID"
)

model_structure_rows <- vector(
  "list",
  length(model_order)
)

for (model_index in seq_along(model_order)) {
  model <- model_order[model_index]

  if (model %in% expected_gblup_models) {
    result_data <- gr[gr$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
    prediction_data <- gp[gp$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
  } else {
    result_data <- ar[ar$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
    prediction_data <- ap[ap$Model == model, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  result_task_key <- do.call(
    paste,
    c(result_data[split_keys], sep = "__")
  )
  prediction_task_key <- do.call(
    paste,
    c(prediction_data[split_keys], sep = "__")
  )
  predictions_per_task <- table(prediction_task_key)

  model_structure_rows[[model_index]] <- data.frame(
    Model = model,
    Tasks = length(unique(result_task_key)),
    Predictions = nrow(prediction_data),
    Min_predictions_per_task = min(predictions_per_task),
    Max_predictions_per_task = max(predictions_per_task),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

model_structure <- do.call(rbind, model_structure_rows)
rownames(model_structure) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(model_structure) == 7L,
  all(model_structure$Tasks == 150L),
  all(model_structure$Predictions == 30000L),
  all(model_structure$Min_predictions_per_task == 200L),
  all(model_structure$Max_predictions_per_task == 200L)
)

model_structure |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Observed task and assessment structure for the seven methods",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

all_predictions <- rbind(
  gp[, c(prediction_keys, "Model", "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value")],
  ap[, c(prediction_keys, "Model", "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value")]
)

reference_model <- model_order[1]
reference_targets <- all_predictions[
  all_predictions$Model == reference_model,
  c(prediction_keys, "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value"),
  drop = FALSE
]

target_match_rows <- vector("list", length(model_order) - 1L)

for (model_index in seq_along(model_order[-1])) {
  model <- model_order[-1][model_index]
  candidate_targets <- all_predictions[
    all_predictions$Model == model,
    c(prediction_keys, "Observed_Phenotype", "True_Genetic_Value"),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  matched_targets <- merge(
    reference_targets,
    candidate_targets,
    by = prediction_keys,
    suffixes = c("_Reference", "_Candidate"),
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )

  stopifnot(nrow(matched_targets) == 30000L)

  target_match_rows[[model_index]] <- data.frame(
    Reference = reference_model,
    Model = model,
    Phenotype_difference = max(abs(
      matched_targets$Observed_Phenotype_Reference -
        matched_targets$Observed_Phenotype_Candidate
    )),
    TrueG_difference = max(abs(
      matched_targets$True_Genetic_Value_Reference -
        matched_targets$True_Genetic_Value_Candidate
    )),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

target_match <- do.call(rbind, target_match_rows)

stopifnot(
  all(target_match$Phenotype_difference == 0),
  all(target_match$TrueG_difference == 0)
)

target_match |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 12,
    caption = paste("Maximum paired target difference relative to", reference_model),
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Every model contributes 150 tasks with 200 held-out predictions per task. The
maximum paired differences in phenotype and true genetic value are zero, so the
methods are evaluated on identical targets for identical held-out individuals.

## 3. Evaluation metrics

M03, M04, and M05 use the same held-out evaluation contract.

- **Pearson correlation** measures linear association between prediction and
  target; larger values are better.
- **Spearman correlation** measures monotonic rank association between prediction
  and target; larger values are better.
- **RMSE** and **MAE** measure prediction error on the original target scale;
  smaller values are better.
- **Bias** is `mean(prediction - target)` and is retained as a secondary
  calibration diagnostic; values nearer zero are preferable.
- **Slope** is the prediction coefficient in `lm(target ~ prediction)` and is
  retained as a secondary calibration diagnostic; values nearer one are
  preferable.
- No \(R^2\) metric is used.

For the simulated benchmark, the known true genetic value is the primary
evaluation target. Therefore the matched pairwise comparisons use exactly four
primary genetic metrics: Pearson, Spearman, RMSE, and MAE. Phenotype metrics and
the Bias/Slope diagnostics remain available for descriptive summaries but are
not included in the pairwise performance-contrast table.

```{r metric-definitions, include=FALSE}
metrics <- c(
  "Genetic_Pearson",
  "Genetic_Spearman",
  "Genetic_RMSE",
  "Genetic_MAE",
  "Genetic_Bias",
  "Genetic_Slope",
  "Phenotype_Pearson",
  "Phenotype_Spearman",
  "Phenotype_RMSE",
  "Phenotype_MAE",
  "Phenotype_Bias",
  "Phenotype_Slope"
)

pairwise_metrics <- c(
  "Genetic_Pearson",
  "Genetic_Spearman",
  "Genetic_RMSE",
  "Genetic_MAE"
)

higher_better <- c(
  "Genetic_Pearson",
  "Genetic_Spearman",
  "Phenotype_Pearson",
  "Phenotype_Spearman"
)

lower_better <- c(
  "Genetic_RMSE",
  "Genetic_MAE",
  "Phenotype_RMSE",
  "Phenotype_MAE"
)

zero_target <- c(
  "Genetic_Bias",
  "Phenotype_Bias"
)

one_target <- c(
  "Genetic_Slope",
  "Phenotype_Slope"
)
```

For a pair of methods, positive performance advantage favors `Model_1`.
Higher-is-better metrics use `Model_1 - Model_2`; lower-is-better metrics use
`Model_2 - Model_1`.

## 4. Overall model performance

### 4.1 Overall means

```{r overall-performance}
analysis_cols <- c(
  "Scenario",
  "Repetition",
  "Fold",
  "SplitID",
  "TaskID",
  "Model",
  metrics
)

all_results <- rbind(
  gr[, analysis_cols],
  ar[, analysis_cols]
)

overall <- aggregate(
  all_results[, metrics],
  by = list(
    Model = all_results$Model
  ),
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

overall <- overall[
  match(
    model_order,
    overall$Model
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

overall_genetic_display <- overall[
  ,
  c(
    "Model",
    "Genetic_Pearson",
    "Genetic_Spearman",
    "Genetic_RMSE",
    "Genetic_MAE",
    "Genetic_Bias",
    "Genetic_Slope"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

overall_genetic_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Overall held-out performance against true genetic value",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

overall_phenotype_display <- overall[
  ,
  c(
    "Model",
    "Phenotype_Pearson",
    "Phenotype_Spearman",
    "Phenotype_RMSE",
    "Phenotype_MAE",
    "Phenotype_Bias",
    "Phenotype_Slope"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

overall_phenotype_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Secondary held-out performance against observed phenotype",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

best_pearson_model <- overall$Model[
  which.max(
    overall$Genetic_Pearson
  )
]
best_pearson_value <- max(
  overall$Genetic_Pearson,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

best_spearman_model <- overall$Model[
  which.max(
    overall$Genetic_Spearman
  )
]
best_spearman_value <- max(
  overall$Genetic_Spearman,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

best_rmse_model <- overall$Model[
  which.min(
    overall$Genetic_RMSE
  )
]
best_rmse_value <- min(
  overall$Genetic_RMSE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

best_mae_model <- overall$Model[
  which.min(
    overall$Genetic_MAE
  )
]
best_mae_value <- min(
  overall$Genetic_MAE,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

ann_overall <- overall[
  overall$Model %in%
    expected_ann_models,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

Across the matched outer tasks, **`r best_pearson_model`** has the highest mean
genetic Pearson correlation (`r sprintf("%.4f", best_pearson_value)`),
**`r best_spearman_model`** has the highest mean genetic Spearman correlation
(`r sprintf("%.4f", best_spearman_value)`), **`r best_rmse_model`** has the
lowest mean genetic RMSE (`r sprintf("%.4f", best_rmse_value)`), and
**`r best_mae_model`** has the lowest mean genetic MAE
(`r sprintf("%.4f", best_mae_value)`). These summaries are descriptive results
for the evaluated models under the frozen validation design.

### 4.2 Distribution across outer tasks

The next figures show the 150 outer-task values for each method. Because the
repeated cross-validation tasks overlap in their training and assessment
samples, these distributions describe sensitivity to the held-out samples; they
are not interpreted as 150 statistically independent replicates.

```{r genetic-correlation-figure, fig.cap="Held-out true genetic-value Pearson correlation across the 150 outer tasks for each of the seven genomic prediction methods. Boxes summarize the task distribution; white diamonds indicate model means."}
plot_results <- all_results
plot_results$Model <- factor(
  plot_results$Model,
  levels = model_order,
  labels = model_labels
)

p_model_correlation <- ggplot(
  plot_results,
  aes(
    x = Model,
    y = Genetic_Pearson,
    fill = Model
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.58,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    alpha = 0.70
  ) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.10,
      height = 0,
      seed = 20260821L + 501L
    ),
    alpha = 0.32,
    size = 1.3
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 3.2,
    fill = "white"
  ) +
  scale_fill_gdocs() +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pearson correlation with true genetic value",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_gdocs() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 20,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

print(p_model_correlation)
```

```{r save-model-correlation-tiff, include=FALSE}

## 5. Performance by scenario

The scenario summary asks whether the overall pattern persists across C1-C6.
These scenarios jointly vary genetic complexity and nominal heritability, so
the sequence is not interpreted as the isolated causal effect of either
quantity.

```{r scenario-performance}
scenario_summary <- aggregate(
  all_results[, metrics],
  by = list(
    Scenario = all_results$Scenario,
    Model = all_results$Model
  ),
  FUN = mean,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

scenario_summary <- scenario_summary[
  order(
    scenario_summary$Scenario,
    match(
      scenario_summary$Model,
      model_order
    )
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

scenario_display <- scenario_summary[
  ,
  c(
    "Scenario",
    "Model",
    "Genetic_Pearson",
    "Genetic_Spearman",
    "Genetic_RMSE",
    "Genetic_MAE"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

scenario_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Primary genetic-value prediction metrics by scenario",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

scenario_ids <- sort(
  unique(
    scenario_summary$Scenario
  )
)

scenario_winner_rows <- vector(
  "list",
  length(
    scenario_ids
  )
)

for (
  scenario_index in
    seq_along(
      scenario_ids
    )
) {
  scenario <- scenario_ids[
    scenario_index
  ]

  scenario_data <- scenario_summary[
    scenario_summary$Scenario ==
      scenario,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  scenario_winner_rows[[
    scenario_index
  ]] <- data.frame(
    Scenario = scenario,
    Best_Pearson =
      scenario_data$Model[
        which.max(
          scenario_data$Genetic_Pearson
        )
      ],
    Best_Spearman =
      scenario_data$Model[
        which.max(
          scenario_data$Genetic_Spearman
        )
      ],
    Best_RMSE =
      scenario_data$Model[
        which.min(
          scenario_data$Genetic_RMSE
        )
      ],
    Best_MAE =
      scenario_data$Model[
        which.min(
          scenario_data$Genetic_MAE
        )
      ],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

scenario_winners <- do.call(
  rbind,
  scenario_winner_rows
)

scenario_win_summary <- data.frame(
  Model = model_order,
  Pearson_wins = vapply(
    model_order,
    function(model) {
      sum(
        scenario_winners$Best_Pearson ==
          model
      )
    },
    integer(1)
  ),
  Spearman_wins = vapply(
    model_order,
    function(model) {
      sum(
        scenario_winners$Best_Spearman ==
          model
      )
    },
    integer(1)
  ),
  RMSE_wins = vapply(
    model_order,
    function(model) {
      sum(
        scenario_winners$Best_RMSE ==
          model
      )
    },
    integer(1)
  ),
  MAE_wins = vapply(
    model_order,
    function(model) {
      sum(
        scenario_winners$Best_MAE ==
          model
      )
    },
    integer(1)
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

scenario_win_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    caption = "Number of scenario-level wins for each primary genetic metric",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

Scenario-level winners are descriptive summaries only. They do not treat the
six scenarios or the repeated outer folds as independent inferential
replicates.

## 6. Pairwise matched contrasts among all methods

All 21 unordered pairs formed by the seven methods are compared within the same
outer split. Positive performance advantage favors `Model_1`; negative values
favor `Model_2`.

### 6.1 Overall pairwise matched contrasts

```{r matched-contrasts}
model_pairs <- t(combn(model_order, 2))
colnames(model_pairs) <- c("Model_1", "Model_2")
stopifnot(nrow(model_pairs) == 21L)

pairwise_rows <- list()
pairwise_row_index <- 0L

for (pair_index in seq_len(nrow(model_pairs))) {
  model_1 <- model_pairs[pair_index, "Model_1"]
  model_2 <- model_pairs[pair_index, "Model_2"]

  x <- all_results[
    all_results$Model == model_1,
    c(split_keys, metrics),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  y <- all_results[
    all_results$Model == model_2,
    c(split_keys, metrics),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  matched <- merge(
    x,
    y,
    by = split_keys,
    suffixes = c("_1", "_2"),
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(matched) == 150L)

  for (metric in pairwise_metrics) {
    value_1 <- matched[[paste0(metric, "_1")]]
    value_2 <- matched[[paste0(metric, "_2")]]
    finite <- is.finite(value_1) & is.finite(value_2)
    value_1 <- value_1[finite]
    value_2 <- value_2[finite]
    raw_difference <- value_1 - value_2

    if (metric %in% higher_better) {
      advantage <- value_1 - value_2
    } else if (metric %in% lower_better) {
      advantage <- value_2 - value_1
    } else if (metric %in% zero_target) {
      advantage <- abs(value_2) - abs(value_1)
    } else {
      advantage <- abs(value_2 - 1) - abs(value_1 - 1)
    }

    pairwise_row_index <- pairwise_row_index + 1L
    pairwise_rows[[pairwise_row_index]] <- data.frame(
      Model_1 = model_1,
      Model_2 = model_2,
      Metric = metric,
      N = length(advantage),
      Mean_Model_1 = mean(value_1),
      Mean_Model_2 = mean(value_2),
      Mean_raw_difference = mean(raw_difference),
      Median_raw_difference = median(raw_difference),
      Mean_performance_advantage = mean(advantage),
      Median_performance_advantage = median(advantage),
      Model_1_better = sum(advantage > 0),
      Equal = sum(advantage == 0),
      Model_2_better = sum(advantage < 0),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
}

pairwise <- do.call(rbind, pairwise_rows)
rownames(pairwise) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(pairwise) == 21L * length(pairwise_metrics),
  all(pairwise$N > 0L),
  all(pairwise$N <= 150L)
)

pairwise_primary <- pairwise[
  pairwise$Metric %in% pairwise_metrics,
  c(
    "Model_1", "Model_2", "Metric", "N",
    "Mean_Model_1", "Mean_Model_2", "Mean_performance_advantage",
    "Model_1_better", "Equal", "Model_2_better"
  )
]
stopifnot(nrow(pairwise_primary) == nrow(model_pairs) * length(pairwise_metrics))

pairwise_primary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Matched pairwise contrasts among all seven methods for primary genetic-value metrics; positive advantage favors Model_1",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

`Model_1_better` and `Model_2_better` count matched outer tasks, so every
comparison uses the same held-out sample for both methods. These counts describe
how often one method performs better within the repeated cross-validation
design; they are not used as independent observations for a naive fold-level
significance test.

### 6.2 Pairwise matched contrasts by scenario

```{r matched-contrasts-by-scenario}
pairwise_scenario_rows <- list()
pairwise_scenario_index <- 0L

for (pair_index in seq_len(nrow(model_pairs))) {
  model_1 <- model_pairs[pair_index, "Model_1"]
  model_2 <- model_pairs[pair_index, "Model_2"]

  x <- all_results[
    all_results$Model == model_1,
    c(split_keys, metrics),
    drop = FALSE
  ]
  y <- all_results[
    all_results$Model == model_2,
    c(split_keys, metrics),
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  matched <- merge(
    x,
    y,
    by = split_keys,
    suffixes = c("_1", "_2"),
    all = FALSE,
    sort = FALSE
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(matched) == 150L)

  for (scenario in sort(unique(matched$Scenario))) {
    scenario_data <- matched[matched$Scenario == scenario, , drop = FALSE]
    stopifnot(nrow(scenario_data) == 25L)

    for (metric in pairwise_metrics) {
      value_1 <- scenario_data[[paste0(metric, "_1")]]
      value_2 <- scenario_data[[paste0(metric, "_2")]]
      finite <- is.finite(value_1) & is.finite(value_2)
      value_1 <- value_1[finite]
      value_2 <- value_2[finite]

      if (metric %in% higher_better) {
        advantage <- value_1 - value_2
      } else if (metric %in% lower_better) {
        advantage <- value_2 - value_1
      } else if (metric %in% zero_target) {
        advantage <- abs(value_2) - abs(value_1)
      } else {
        advantage <- abs(value_2 - 1) - abs(value_1 - 1)
      }

      pairwise_scenario_index <- pairwise_scenario_index + 1L
      pairwise_scenario_rows[[pairwise_scenario_index]] <- data.frame(
        Scenario = scenario,
        Model_1 = model_1,
        Model_2 = model_2,
        Metric = metric,
        N = length(advantage),
        Mean_advantage = mean(advantage),
        Median_advantage = median(advantage),
        Model_1_better = sum(advantage > 0),
        Equal = sum(advantage == 0),
        Model_2_better = sum(advantage < 0),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  }
}

pairwise_scenario <- do.call(rbind, pairwise_scenario_rows)
rownames(pairwise_scenario) <- NULL

stopifnot(
  nrow(pairwise_scenario) == nrow(model_pairs) * length(scenario_ids) * length(pairwise_metrics),
  all(pairwise_scenario$N > 0L),
  all(pairwise_scenario$N <= 25L)
)

pairwise_scenario_primary <- pairwise_scenario[
  pairwise_scenario$Metric %in% pairwise_metrics,
  c(
    "Scenario", "Model_1", "Model_2", "Metric", "N", "Mean_advantage",
    "Model_1_better", "Equal", "Model_2_better"
  )
]
stopifnot(nrow(pairwise_scenario_primary) == nrow(model_pairs) * length(scenario_ids) * length(pairwise_metrics))

pairwise_scenario_primary |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Matched pairwise advantages by scenario for the four primary genetic-value metrics; positive values favor Model_1",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )
```

The scenario-level contrasts show whether pairwise differences are concentrated
in a subset of simulation conditions or recur across the full C1-C6 sequence.
They remain descriptive summaries of matched held-out tasks.

## 7. Regularization within the ANN branch

The four ANN variants share, within each outer task, the architecture and
learning rate selected with ANN_0 in M04. Their overall contrast therefore
describes the effect associated with the evaluated L1/L2 choices **conditional
on that shared structural selection rule**.

```{r ann-regularization}
ann_regularization_display <- overall[
  match(
    expected_ann_models,
    overall$Model
  ),
  c(
    "Model",
    "Genetic_Pearson",
    "Genetic_Spearman",
    "Genetic_RMSE",
    "Genetic_MAE"
  ),
  drop = FALSE
]

ann_regularization_display |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "html",
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Overall primary genetic-value performance among ANN variants",
    row.names = FALSE,
    table.attr = 'class="table table-striped table-hover table-bordered"'
  )

ann_l1 <- ann_overall[
  ann_overall$Model == "ANN_L1",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
ann_l1_l2 <- ann_overall[
  ann_overall$Model == "ANN_L1_L2",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
ann_l2 <- ann_overall[
  ann_overall$Model == "ANN_L2",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
ann_0 <- ann_overall[
  ann_overall$Model == "ANN_0",
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
```

ANN-L1+L2 has the strongest overall ANN averages by a very small margin over
ANN-L1: genetic Pearson correlation is
`r sprintf("%.4f", ann_l1_l2$Genetic_Pearson)` versus
`r sprintf("%.4f", ann_l1$Genetic_Pearson)`, and genetic RMSE is
`r sprintf("%.4f", ann_l1_l2$Genetic_RMSE)` versus
`r sprintf("%.4f", ann_l1$Genetic_RMSE)`. ANN-L2 remains close to ANN-0
(correlations `r sprintf("%.4f", ann_l2$Genetic_Pearson)` and
`r sprintf("%.4f", ann_0$Genetic_Pearson)`, respectively). Within the
prespecified ANN search, the observed regularization gain is therefore associated
mainly with the L1 component.

## 8. Scientific conclusion

Within the prespecified simulated-data benchmark, model performance is evaluated
with four primary held-out metrics against the known true genetic value:
Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, RMSE, and MAE. Bias and calibration
slope are retained as secondary diagnostics, and no \(R^2\) metric is used.

The seven methods are compared on the same frozen outer splits. All 21 unordered
method pairs are evaluated within matched outer tasks, so no GBLUP or ANN method
is privileged as the universal reference. The overall and scenario summaries
describe the observed performance within the evaluated simulation conditions
and prespecified model-search spaces; they do not establish a universal ranking
between genomic mixed models and neural networks.

```{r comparison-output-contract, include=FALSE}
WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS <- identical(
  Sys.getenv("WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS", "0"),
  "1"
)

COMPARISON_DIR <- "output/simulated/comparison"
OVERALL_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "simulated_model_overall_summary.csv"
)
SCENARIO_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "simulated_model_scenario_summary.csv"
)
PAIRWISE_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "simulated_model_pairwise_summary.csv"
)
PAIRWISE_SCENARIO_CSV <- file.path(
  COMPARISON_DIR,
  "simulated_model_pairwise_by_scenario.csv"
)
```

```{r write-comparison-outputs, eval=WRITE_COMPARISON_OUTPUTS, include=FALSE}

  COMPARISON_DIR,
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)
write.csv(overall, OVERALL_CSV, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(scenario_summary, SCENARIO_CSV, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pairwise, PAIRWISE_CSV, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(pairwise_scenario, PAIRWISE_SCENARIO_CSV, row.names = FALSE)
```
